title: Who Have I Reduced?
headline: Seeing People the Way God Sees Them
tagline: Every difficult person has a history you haven’t lived.
seo_title: How to See People the Way God Sees Them (1 Samuel 16:7) | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Before asking God to change how you treat people, ask Him to change how you see them. A devotional for men on 1 Samuel 16:7 and abiding in Christ.
verse_text: The Lord does not look at the things people look at. People look at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.

scriptures.text: The Lord does not look at the things people look at. People look at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.

items: Before asking God to change how you treat people….
ask Him to change how you see them.
Because behavior follows vision.
And vision is formed by where we continually fix our attention.
Jesus teaches in John 15 that branches don’t produce fruit by striving harder.
They bear fruit by remaining connected to the Vine.
As we remain in Him, He doesn’t simply change what we do.
He changes what we see.
Think about the last person who frustrated you.
Have you been viewing them primarily through annoyance, disappointment, judgment, inconvenience, past experiences or what they did?
Or have you remembered they are someone Christ loves….
someone made in His image….
someone Christ died to redeem?
God looks deeper.
He sees the fears no one knows.
The wounds no one notices.
The battles no one talks about.
The burdens they’ve hidden.
Every difficult person has a history you haven’t lived.
Every reaction has a story behind it.
Abiding with Christ slowly teaches us to look beneath the surface.
To pause before judging.
To become curious before becoming critical.
We rarely struggle to love people because we know too much about them.
We struggle because we see too little of them.
